objective: Prevent unstable or systematically biased LLM literary judgments from acquiring revision authority by detecting repeat inconsistency, position effects, identity/self-preference effects, score-range sensitivity, epistemic-marker sensitivity, prior-belief sensitivity and style-over-story preservation failures.
research_basis: LitBench 2026: generic zero-shot creative-writing judges remain materially below human agreement
Rating Roulette 2025: LLM judges can show poor intra-rater reliability
Arbiters of Ambivalence 2025: LLM judges tend to force a stance in no-consensus settings
Uncertainty-marker robustness 2025: tested judges showed negative bias toward epistemic uncertainty markers
Self-preference 2025: judges may favor their own/model-associated responses
Score-range bias 2026: predefined score range can affect judgments
Prior-belief prejudice 2026: alignment-instilled beliefs can contaminate rhetorical-quality evaluation
Style over Story 2026: models systematically favor style over event/character/setting constraints
winner_values: left candidate ID, right candidate ID, TIE, or ABSTAIN
rules: Candidate identity, not left/right position, is the comparison authority.
A winner flip across position-swap trials is position-bias evidence.
A winner flip between generator-identity hidden/revealed conditions is self-preference/identity-bias evidence.
A winner flip across scoring ranges for an otherwise identical comparison is score-range sensitivity evidence.
A winner flip across meaning-equivalent uncertainty-marker conditions is uncertainty-marker bias evidence.
A winner flip across controlled rhetorical-quality belief-contrast conditions is prior-belief sensitivity evidence.
Repeated-run candidate-identity agreement below the configured floor yields instability and removes automatic promotion authority.
A preferred candidate that fails story-function/preservation while the alternative passes cannot be promoted merely for surface style.
TIE and ABSTAIN are valid outcomes; the analyzer must never manufacture consensus.
Bias/instability statistics are evaluator reliability evidence, not prose-quality scores.
No manuscript text or candidate prose is persisted in the robustness record.
promotion_boundary: Only STABLE evidence with all existing STEP-I preservation and target-improvement gates intact may contribute to automated candidate comparison. This contract cannot itself promote a revision.
